messages:
alex: Heads-up: EU ingress saw a single tenant produce long-running streams that clogged the frontdoor queues during peak. P95 spiked. Proposing a non-blocking tenant-shed filter.

sasha: Curious: do we want deterministic caps or a smoother probabilistic approach? Deterministic is simpler to reason about but can cause unused capacity.

yun: Streaming semantics mean we must avoid killing midstream. Admission must be at request start, with classification for short vs long.

alex: Proposed pattern: at request start, estimate token cost; maintain per-tenant sliding-window tokens (approx counters). If over-budget, apply probabilistic admission proportional to remaining budget. If admitted and long, charge incrementally. On drop emit header X-RW-SHED: retry-after=150 so SDKs can back off.

sasha: Also consider reservoir weighting based on recent sustained share so big tenants don't hog transient bursts. Keep small guaranteed floors for paid tiers.

yun: Implementation notes: implement as a lightweight ingress hook (C++) to minimize latency. Add trace tag shed=1 for observability. Collect metrics: p95 small-tenant latency, token-throttle-rate, KV-cache-hit-delta.

alex: I'll write an RFC with pseudocode and rollout gating. sasha: can you add a sim using last-quarter traces? yun: please wire header+trace support. infra-bot: create ticket.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-8423: tenant-shed-filter experiment (probabilistic admits + long-stream safeguards).
